title: Platform-wide slowness and 429s
executive_summary: INC-011 (SEV2) was a platform-wide latency and HTTP 429 incident affecting api-gateway, auth-service, and user-service, with symptoms starting at 2026-10-02T20:00Z. The investigation reached status ROOT_CAUSE_IDENTIFIED with a leading hypothesis of a traffic surge entering api-gateway (confidence 0.88). Gateway request rate rose about 129% from baseline starting 19:55Z (met-api-gateway-request_rate-1930-2025), and auth-service and user-service request rates rose by a similar 123-125% in the same bucket (met-auth-service-request_rate-1930-2025, met-user-service-request_rate-1930-2025). CPU climbed to roughly 86% on auth-service and 71% on user-service (met-auth-service-cpu_pct-1930-2025, met-user-service-cpu_pct-1930-2025), and user-service p95 latency rose from about 81 ms to about 398 ms mean (met-user-service-p95_latency_ms-1930-2025). The gateway then returned 429s to clients, starting 19:56:06Z (logpat-api-gateway-8a499a8e), and gateway error rate rose from about 0.5% to about 3.9% mean, peaking at 7.6% (met-api-gateway-error_rate-1930-2025). The most probable explanation is a client-side retry storm from the mobile-ios-7.4.0 client population, which began at 19:55:11Z and ignored Retry-After headers, according to the validation critic's review of gateway logs. The reason the retries began (client release, upstream error, or other) was not established. The 7.1.3 user-service deployment at 19:48Z was a copy-only change and was rejected as a cause (dep-78c036fc, H2).

hypotheses.description: An unidentified upstream caller or client population increased request volume into api-gateway at ~19:55Z (about 2.3x). The extra load propagated to auth-service and user-service, saturating their CPU and raising p95 latency. The gateway then rate-limited some clients, producing 429s and the error-rate rise. Mechanism: External or caller-side traffic increase at the ingress (api-gateway request_rate +129%, onset 19:55Z) -> auth-service and user-service request rates rise by a similar ~123-125% in the same bucket -> CPU rises to ~75-86% (auth) and ~65-71% (user) -> p95 latency rises 4-7x at 19:56Z -> gateway/upstream saturation and per-client rate limiting return 429s and push gateway error rate from ~0.5% to ~7%.

critic_review.summary: H1 (traffic surge entering api-gateway from 19:55Z, with gateway rate-limiting producing 429s) is well supported and the open question in its missing_evidence is now largely answered. Gateway logs identify the source: client_id=mobile-ios-7.4.0 is the top client, rising from ~1700 rps to ~9500 rps, and the rate limiter reports that 363-396% of its requests are retries with Retry-After ignored. This is a client-side retry storm that starts at 19:55:11Z, before the first 429 at 19:56:06Z. The gateway ingress, auth-service, and user-service steps all fall in the same 19:55Z bucket, which fits propagation from the ingress. Refinement: the culprit is the mobile-ios-7.4.0 client population's retry behaviour, not a service in the platform, so the culprit_service label 'api-gateway' should be read as the ingress where the surge lands. H2 is rejected: the 7.1.3 deploy at 19:48Z is the only deployment in the window and is a copy-only change. The gateway ingress rose by the same amount, and auth-service has no dependency on user-service, so user-service cannot be the source of the step. H3 is rejected: postgres CPU, connections, and p95 are flat, and payment and order request rates are flat, so they do not show the surge. Remaining limitations: what triggered the mobile-ios-7.4.0 retries (client release, upstream error, or other) is not established, and the 7% gateway error rate is not broken down by status code. Neither blocks the category or culprit conclusion.

assessments.reasoning: Gateway logs name the source of the step: client_id=mobile-ios-7.4.0, 1700 rps rising to 9500 rps, with 363-396% retries and Retry-After ignored, starting 19:55:11Z before the first 429 at 19:56:06Z. The ingress, auth, and user steps share the 19:55Z bucket. Notification and payment are flat, and postgres is flat. The surge is a client-side retry storm; the 'api-gateway' culprit label is the ingress where it lands.

The 7.1.3 deploy at 19:48Z is copy-only and is the only deployment in the window. The ingress rate, which a user-service change cannot raise, steps up by the same amount. auth-service has no dependency on user-service, and its rise is unexplained by this hypothesis.

postgres CPU, db connection utilisation, and p95 latency are all flat versus baseline. user-service DB connections are unchanged. The only support is a log pattern of long report_rollup statements, which does not match the metric picture. Payment and order traffic are also flat.

root_cause_statement: ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED (critic-approved; still an INFERENCE from evidence): traffic_surge in api-gateway - An unidentified upstream caller or client population increased request volume into api-gateway at ~19:55Z (about 2.3x). The extra load propagated to auth-service and user-service, saturating their CPU and raising p95 latency. The gateway then rate-limited some clients, producing 429s and the error-rate rise.
corrective_actions: Reduce the inbound retry load from the mobile-ios-7.4.0 client population: apply per-client throttling or temporary rate limits that honor Retry-After, and confirm 429 rates fall (logpat-api-gateway-8a499a8e).
Engage the mobile team to identify whether a recent 7.4.0 client build or an upstream error is driving retries, and ship a fix or server-side override if one is found.
Monitor auth-service and user-service CPU and p95 latency until they return to baseline (about 30% CPU and about 81 ms p95) after throttling takes effect.
preventive_actions: Enforce client-side exponential backoff with jitter and Retry-After compliance in mobile SDKs, and verify compliance in pre-release testing for client versions.
Add gateway-level retry budgets and per-client quotas so a single client population cannot saturate downstream auth and user services.
Set capacity headroom or autoscaling for auth-service and user-service so a roughly 2.3x ingress increase does not drive CPU above about 85%.
Add client_id and version as dimensions in gateway request metrics to speed up attribution in future incidents.
monitoring_recommendations: Alert when api-gateway request_rate exceeds 1.5x its 7-day baseline for more than 2 minutes, and when any single client_id exceeds 2x its own baseline.
Alert on the gateway 429 count and the ratio of retried requests (retries per original request above 1.5 with Retry-After ignored).
Alert on gateway error_rate above 1% for 5 minutes, and break down errors by status code to confirm the 429 share of the 7% peak.
Alert on auth-service and user-service CPU above 70% and p95 latency above 3x baseline, with dashboards that show the request rate step alongside them.
Track postgres CPU, connection utilization, and p95 latency as a control signal to confirm the database is not contributing.
limitations: Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
Investigation terminated because: critic verdict APPROVED
conclusion: The most probable root cause is a traffic surge at the api-gateway ingress, driven by retry behavior from the mobile-ios-7.4.0 client population beginning at 19:55Z. This surge saturated auth-service and user-service and led the gateway to return 429s. The user-service 7.1.3 deployment and the postgres report_rollup queries were ruled out. The trigger for the client retry storm is not established, and the status-code breakdown of the gateway error rate is still needed to fully confirm that 429s account for the increase. These gaps do not change the category or culprit conclusion, and follow-up work should focus on the client trigger and on preventing retry storms from saturating downstream services.
